mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study examines the asymmetric and state-dependent effects of exchange rate movements on money demand in six developed economies (Australia, Canada, the Euro Area, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States) using quarterly data from 1970Q1 to 2025Q1. Linear ARDL and nonlinear ARDL (NARDL) models are employed alongside quantile ARDL (QARDL) to capture asymmetry and distributional heterogeneity. The ARDL results confirm a stable long-run relationship between money demand and its determinants, while NARDL estimates reveal pronounced asymmetries between appreciations and depreciations, consistent with patterns attributable to substitution and wealth effects. These effects are stronger and more consistent for M3 than M1, reflecting broader portfolio adjustments. Quantile results indicate that exchange rate effects are highly state-dependent, intensifying at the tails of the distribution. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of nonlinear, state-dependent modeling and the relevance of broad money aggregates in monetary policy analysis.

A modified Jaeger’s Plane of Weakness model, incorporating the effects of asperity ratio (),, and, is proposed. mods:mods.mods:abstract: We present a Riccati-based framework for safety-critical nonlinear control that integrates the barrier states (BaS) methodology with the State-Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) approach. The BaS formulation embeds safety constraints into the system dynamics via auxiliary states, enabling safety to be treated as a control objective. To overcome the limited region of attraction in linear BaS controllers, we extend the framework to nonlinear systems using SDRE synthesis applied to the barrier-augmented dynamics and derive a matrix inequality condition that certifies forward invariance of a large region of attraction and guarantees asymptotic safe stabilization. The resulting controller is computed online via point-wise Riccati solutions. We validate the method on an unstable constrained system and cluttered quadrotor navigation tasks, demonstrating improved constraint handling, scalability, and robustness near safety boundaries. This framework offers a principled and computationally tractable solution for synthesizing nonlinear safe feedback in safety-critical environments.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources (RERs) in modern power grids has significantly reduced system inertia, which poses serious challenges to frequency stability. In addition, system uncertainties can significantly affect frequency regulation, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a coordinated control strategy for enhancing frequency stability in low-inertia power systems. The proposed strategy controller integrates load frequency control based on an active disturbance rejection control in combination with linear quadratic Gaussian (ADRC–LQG) controller and a virtual damping stabilization (VDS-ESS). The proposed LFC (ADRC–LQG) controller has the benefits of optimal control and real-time disturbance rejection, while the VDS-ESS part provides additional damping to compensate for loss of grid inertia. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed LFC (ADRC–LQG) controller outperforms other controllers like TD-TI, PD-PI, FO-PD-PI, and ADRC. Furthermore, the coordinated LFC (ADRC–LQG) & VDS-ESS strategy improves frequency deviation performance by up to 65.93% compared with LFC (ADRC–LQG) & VIC-ESS under high renewable penetration. The robustness and sensitivity of the proposed LFC (ADRC–LQG) & VDS-ESS strategy are further validated under false data injection attacks, inertia variations, and communication time delays, confirming its effectiveness in low-inertia power grids.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The rapid, continuous industrialization and discharge of industrial wastewater into the environment are inevitable, and due to the complexity of this wastewater, cleaning up hazardous pollutants, especially heavy metals, is challenging. Adsorption techniques using advanced coordinated porous functional materials such as graphene/graphitic-based metal–organic frameworks (GBMOFs) offer a promising alternative because of their improved properties and multifunctionality. Thus, this review presents a comprehensive recent advance in GBMOFs for adsorptive cleanup of heavy metals. The work underscores the coordination diversity, synthesis methods, and properties of GBMOFs, and identifies key performance trends and patterns, while providing critical insights. The study shows that GBMOFs generally exhibit high adsorption efficiency/capacity over a wide range of operational conditions (pH 3–9, temperature 293–328 K, and dose 2 ≃ 1000 mg) through key GBMOF–heavy metal interactions like coordination, complexation, pore filling, electrostatic, and π–π interactions. Notably, while the recyclability studies revealed that GBMOFs can be reused 3–30 times, concerns regarding environmental safety are still palpable. Additionally, techno-economic analysis and technology readiness level (TRL) show that GBMOFs are still expensive and at TRL1–4. Hence, to advance beyond this level, it is suggested that future research should integrate the use of AI for guiding the design of highly practical and cost-effective GBMOF adsorption systems.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Kagome graphene is a low-density sp2-bonded carbon allotrope in which triangular units and Kagome-like pores form a load-bearing network distinct from graphene's honeycomb lattice. Although its flat-band physics and tensile wrinkling have been discussed, its reliability under thermal, rate, and defect conditions remains unclear. Here, classical molecular dynamics simulations are used to identify how Kagome topology controls stiffness, strength, and fracture. The structure is benchmarked against reported first-principles calculated geometry and a same-protocol graphene control; the AIREBO limitations for this strained network are stated. The model-size analysis is treated as a periodic-cell convergence test, leading to a 32.2 × 32.2 nm cell with room-temperature Young's moduli of 318.08 and 317.70 GPa along the c₂-parallel x and c₁-parallel y directions, and ultimate strengths of 23.31 and 27.21 GPa. Kagome graphene shows pronounced rate-dependent failure, with strain-rate-sensitivity exponents of 0.10265 and 0.07497 in x and y. Temperature is more damaging: increasing from 300 to 900 K reduces strength by 72.0–75.1% and strain-energy density to fracture by 90.1–93.2%. Defects constructed at the same nominal geometric scale show that stiffness loss is governed by removed load-bearing area and ligament continuity, whereas strength and failure strain are controlled by edge orientation and crack-like stress concentration. These mechanisms provide design rules for Kagome-graphene nanodevices and motivate future first-principles or machine-learning-potential fracture studies.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Fatigue is a multidimensional construct associated with reduced productivity and adverse health outcomes. Existing studies fail to capture fatigue comprehensively and reliably, as they focus on isolated aspects of fatigue and rely on fixed biosignal configurations. This study conceptualizes fatigue into three aspects, namely temporal, spatial, and systemic aspects. As biosignals exhibit varying resilience to noise, a reliability-aware biosignals ranking and selection framework, termed Trimodal Correlation (TRI-CORR) was designed to assess mental fatigue adaptively. The framework begins with the acquisition and preprocessing of electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), galvanic skin response (GSR), and photoplethysmography (PPG) data. Three types of correlations that quantify three aspects of fatigue across multimodal biosignals were captured and fed into adaptive classification module containing Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). The framework adaptively weights and ranks the contribution of biosignals based on correlational data for reliable fatigue classification. Performance evaluation on custom dataset demonstrates its effectiveness, achieving 10-fold cross-validation accuracy of 0.882±0.021, test accuracy of 0.757, test F1 of 0.777, and test ROC-AUC of 0.905. EEG and skin PPG contribute most significantly to the classification, while tree-based LightGBM demonstrates strong capability in learning correlation-derived features. Increasing the time window size, number of fatigue aspects and biosignals improve classification performance. In the cross-dataset validation on the publicly available Mental Fatigue Assessment through Neurophysiological and Biosignal Data (MEFAR) dataset against benchmarking approaches, the proposed framework demonstrates competitive performance, achieving 10-fold cross-validation accuracy of 0.9810, test accuracy of 0.9653, test F1 of 0.9650, and test ROC-AUC of 0.9959.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study examines the factors influencing Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) across G-20 countries from 1990 to 2023, focusing on macroeconomic, demographic, infrastructural, and sustainability-related drivers. Using the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator, along with Mean Group (MG) and Common Correlated Effects (CCE) estimates for robustness, the analysis finds that GDP and debt burden have a negative impact on FDI, indicating that high economic saturation and sovereign risk discourage foreign investment. In contrast, population size, shipping connectivity, human capital, and energy efficiency exhibit a positive influence on FDI, highlighting the importance of market size, infrastructure quality, skilled labor, and sustainable energy practices in attracting foreign capital. The findings challenge the conventional view that larger economies are always more attractive for FDI and underscore the complex relationship between economic growth, sustainability, and investment flows. The study concludes with policy recommendations for G-20 nations to prioritize human capital development, infrastructure improvement, and energy efficiency to foster sustainable FDI and maintain global competitiveness.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This article presents a computationally efficient maximum power point tracking (MPPT) strategy for high-power permanent-magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind energy conversion systems (WECSs). A reduced-input fuzzy controller (RFC) is developed by transforming a conventional dual-input fuzzy controller (DFC) into a single-input structure through a signed-distance formulation that combines the error and change-of-error variables into a unified control signal. The proposed transformation reduces the fuzzy rule base from 49 to 7 rules, corresponding to an 85.7% reduction in inference requirements, while preserving the control characteristics of the original DFC. The controller is implemented on a 2 MW WECS employing a three-phase interleaved boost converter (IBC) and evaluated under identical operating conditions against the DFC and previously benchmarked heuristic MPPT methods. Comprehensive simulation studies are conducted under varying wind profiles, including turbulent and low-wind conditions, ±5% sensor noise, ±10% converter parameter variations, reference changes, and transitions between continuous and discontinuous conduction modes (DCMs). Performance is assessed using power-tracking characteristics, ripple analysis, integral error indices, and computational complexity measures. Results show that the RFC maintains MPPT performance comparable to the conventional DFC while reducing controller execution time from 250 to 50 ms, corresponding to an 80% reduction in computational time. In addition, the RFC achieves a 14.3% reduction in power ripple and maintains robust operation under measurement noise, parameter uncertainty, and varying operating conditions. These findings confirm that the proposed RFC provides a practical and resource-efficient MPPT solution suitable for real-time embedded implementation in large-scale wind energy systems.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The rapid advancement of electrochemical energy storage technologies has created an urgent demand for sustainable, high-performance, and safe battery materials. Among renewable biomass resources, cellulose has emerged as a promising candidate because of its abundance, renewability, mechanical robustness, tunable surface chemistry, and excellent affinity for electrolytes. This review first presents a comprehensive overview of cellulose sources, including plant-derived, bacterial, and algal cellulose, and discusses the major extraction approaches used to obtain high-purity cellulose, including chemical, mechanical, and emerging green extraction technologies based on ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, and supercritical fluids. The hierarchical structure of cellulose is then examined from molecular chains and elementary fibrils to microfibrils, macrofibrils, and fiber-level architectures, highlighting how crystalline and amorphous domains are organized within nanofibrillar networks. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between these multiscale structural features and the resulting mechanical strength, ionic transport behavior, thermal stability, electrolyte affinity, and interfacial characteristics. Building on these structure–property relationships, the review systematically analyzes the application of cellulose-based materials in advanced battery systems, including lithium-ion, sodium-ion, potassium-ion, zinc-ion, lithium–sulfur, and solid-state batteries. The multifunctional roles of cellulose as binders, separators, and gel or solid polymer electrolyte frameworks are discussed, with attention to dendrite suppression, electrolyte uptake, interface stabilization, and cycling performance enhancement. Finally, the remaining challenges related to scalability, moisture sensitivity, ion-transport optimization, and standardization are critically evaluated, and future directions for integrating cellulose-based materials into next-generation sustainable energy-storage technologies are outlined.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Accurate and interpretable prediction of vehicular carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions is essential for advancing sustainable transportation and carbon-neutral mobility. This study presents a controlled experimental framework to compare the interpretability, attention allocation, feature sparsity, and learning behavior of TabNet configurations selected by Halfway Escape Optimization (HEO) and Firefighter Optimization (FFO) for vehicular CO2 emission prediction. Rather than focusing solely on predictive accuracy, the study examines differences in feature-attribution patterns, attention concentration, and sparsity behavior between the HEO- and FFO-selected TabNet configurations. The results indicate that the TabNet configurations selected by HEO and FFO exhibit distinct attention-allocation patterns, feature-sparsity structures, and explanation behaviors. While high predictive accuracy is expected due to the strong physical relationship between fuel-consumption variables and CO2 emissions, the primary contribution of this study lies in characterizing differences in interpretability and learning behavior between the HEO- and FFO-selected TabNet configurations. Feature-ablation analysis further confirms this dependence: after removing all fuel-consumption variables, R2 decreased from above 0.99 to approximately 0.94 for both optimized configurations, while substantial predictive information remained in the non-fuel vehicle attributes. Regression Error Characteristic (REC) analysis shows that approximately 93% of test samples fall within a ±10 g/km error threshold. Interpretability analysis indicates that fuel consumption variables and engine size dominate feature attribution, consistent with known physical relationships in the dataset. The alignment between TabNet feature masks and SHAP attributes reflects consistency in feature importance patterns across interpretability methods, rather than causal inference. Overall, this study provides insights into interpretability differences across optimizer-selected TabNet configurations.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized high-gain cavity antenna employing an in-house-fabricated, high-permittivity dielectric superstrate for C-band satellite downlink communication. The superstrate is realized by 3D printing of a host structure, which is subsequently infilled with an equal-proportion mixture of titanium dioxide (TiO2) and water to obtain the required effective permittivity. The high effective permittivity of the developed superstrate enables substantial miniaturization while preserving strong cavity-field enhancement. The overall superstrate dimensions are reduced to 1.56λ0× 1.56λ0, (λ0 is the free-space wavelength at the design frequency of 3.9 GHz). The proposed antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 20.5%, extending from 3.5−4.3 GHz and fully encompassing the conventional C-band satellite downlink spectrum (3.7−4.2 GHz). A peak realized gain of 15.5 dBi and a maximum aperture efficiency of 62% are obtained, demonstrating an improved size-to-gain performance. Compared with the standalone feed antenna, the proposed superstrate-loaded cavity provides an 8 dB gain enhancement, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the high-permittivity loading mechanism. Moreover, the sidelobe levels remain below −13 dB throughout the operating band. A prototype is fabricated and experimentally characterized, with the measured results exhibiting good agreement with full-wave simulations. The compact footprint, high gain, broad bandwidth, and low sidelobe levels make the proposed antenna a promising low-profile alternative to bulky conventional parabolic reflector antennas for space-constrained C-band satellite communication terminals and air/space-platform applications.

Traditional approaches, based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and heuristic algorithms, face significant limitations in scalability and computational efficiency, particularly for large-scale networks. To address these challenges, this work proposes a Machine Learning (ML)-based algorithm that uses clustering and classification techniques to find energy-efficient configurations in Software-Defined Networks, respectively. Simulations on realistic network topologies demonstrate that our solution delivers results close to those achieved by the reference algorithms, and near-optimal performance when ILP-based solutions are used as reference, achieving up to 53% energy savings while reducing execution time by up to 8,000 times. These results highlight the potential of ML-driven approaches to enable scalable and energy-efficient network management.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper analyses least-cost, low-emission electricity pathways for Saudi Arabia over 2018–2040. Using the LEAP modelling framework, four supply pathways are evaluated under a common electricity demand trajectory reaching 640.2 TWh by 2040, requiring approximately 707.4 TWh of electricity generation after accounting for transmission and distribution losses. Reference Scenario (RS), Maximum Natural Gas Scenario (MNGS) and Sustainable Future Scenario (SFS) apply exogenously specified generation portfolios, while the Least-Cost Generation Scenario (LCGS) employs LEAP's integrated optimisation to endogenously select the mix. Results indicate that LCGS delivers the lowest total generation cost (USD 34.7 billion in 2040) and the lowest emissions of 51.1 million metric tons CO2 equivalent (MMtCO₂e), outperforming RS (USD 46.9 billion; 75.2 MMtCO₂e), MNGS (USD 48.6 billion; 71.9 MMtCO₂e) and SFS (USD 58.4 billion; 55.2 MMtCO₂e). For an identical demand outlook, an optimised portfolio reduces both system costs and emissions relative to business-as-usual and technology-biased pathways. The analysis provides transparent cost–carbon trade-offs for capacity-expansion planning and supports cleaner, more affordable electricity development consistent with long-term energy security and Vision 2030 objectives. Conclusions emphasise the value of integrated optimisation to guide the sequencing of investments while indicating that targeted renewables, calibrated gas and nuclear additions, and demand-side measures can jointly improve affordability and decarbonisation outcomes.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Limestone rocks are increasingly being excavated for infrastructures developments and mining projects, and for extracting construction materials. This calls for data and models to be available for practicing engineers to predict mechanical properties of limestone from basic rock indices. This paper aims at addressing this gap by developing statistical models to predict the tensile strength of local limestone, from basic rock indices. The methodology includes experimental work to obtain data of local limestone properties, and statistical analysis to correlate the tensile strength with various rock properties. The experimental study used 100 cylindrical cores for index-property tests and compressive-strength tests, 100 disks for Brazilian tensile-strength strength tests, and 100 prisms for flexural strength tests. Additionally, rock indices were obtained for these samples, including dry density, P-wave velocity, hardness, porosity, specific gravity, water absorption, and point-load strength index, in addition to compressive strength. Statistical analysis includes simple-regression models for interpretable prediction, and machine-learning models used to evaluate nonlinear effects and predictive performance. The machine-learning models achieved repeated tenfold cross-validated R2 of about 0.88 for the Brazilian tensile strength and 0.62 for the flexural tensile strength, and provided distribution-free conformal-prediction intervals for uncertainty-aware use. Results of experimental work are presented for the index properties, the compressive strength, and the tensile strength (Brazilian and flexural). Outcomes of the regression analysis indicated that TB and TF are strongly correlated with the stated index properties, and also TB correlated well with TF. The results compare well with models available in the literature. It can be concluded that the presented models enable the estimation of tensile strength of limestone from index properties that can be obtained from simple, quick, inexpensive, and non-destructive tests.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: In this paper, we study a viscoelastic coupled system that incorporates two distinct mechanisms of energy dissipation: a nonlinear frictional damping of power type and a memory-type viscoelastic damping. Our investigation is inspired by the recent breakthrough of Haraux and Tebou (Energy decay estimates for the wave equation with supercritical nonlinear damping. Math Anal Appl. 2025;550:129622. doi: 10.1016/j.jmaa.2025.129622), who derived sharp decay estimates for wave equations endowed with supercritical nonlinear damping ((Formula presented.)), showing that strong solutions decay at a polynomial rate while weak solutions exhibit logarithmic decay under mild additional conditions. Extending this framework, we examine a viscoelastic system with memory effects, where the interaction between the instantaneous nonlinear damping and the hereditary viscoelastic dissipation introduces new analytical challenges concerning stability and long-time behavior. Under general structural hypotheses on the damping function and the relaxation kernel, we establish general decay results that capture the influence of both mechanisms. In particular, we show that the asymptotic decay rate of the system energy is governed by the interplay between the nonlinear damping exponent, covering the supercritical regime, and the asymptotic profile of the memory kernel.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Purpose – Drawing on social exchange theory and a knowledge management perspective, this study aims to examine whether green leadership fosters green innovative behavior through environmental commitment and green knowledge-sharing behavior. The study also tests whether job autonomy conditions this serial mediation process. Design/methodology/approach – This study employed a quantitative research design, collecting survey data from 384 Generation Z employees in hospitality organizations. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings – Green leadership did not exert a significant direct effect on green innovative behavior, rather, its influence operated through green knowledge-sharing behavior and through the serial path from environmental commitment to green knowledge-sharing behavior. Job autonomy did not strengthen the direct relationship, yet it strengthened the indirect process, indicating a bounded but meaningful contingency role. Originality/value – This study contributes to research on sustainability and knowledge management by showing that green leadership matters for green innovative behavior when it functions as a knowledge-enabling governance mechanism rather than as a direct innovation trigger. Specifically, the study clarifies how environmental commitment and green knowledge-sharing behavior convert leadership signals into green innovative behavior.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) is not the least significant component of the modern industrial, yet the reliable operation of the smart manufacturing environment cannot be guaranteed since the breakdowns of PEMFCs are multiple and highly complex in character. The article describes the UFDL-Edge, an uncertainty-based federated deep learning model that was created to detect the defects of PEMFC in real-time through an IIoT-based manufacturing plant. The objective of the proposed architecture is to offer the adaptive feature detector and an open-ended model evolution without compromising the privacy of the data in the distributed manufacturing locales through integrating uncertainty-aware feature detectors (UFD) with temporal Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS)-based streaming. It employs a hierarchical and federated learning approach to obtain a combination of the advantages of Byzantine-resistant aggregation and uncertainty quantification to enhance the resilience of fault-detection in a variety of operating conditions. The 10.3% improvement in F1-score on the initial anomaly detection, 23.7% reduction in false positive ratio, and less than 100ms latency of real-time diagnostics obtained with huge-scale experimentation in three testbeds of smart manufacturing are better results. Foot printing framework eliminates drastic challenges such as cold start issue, water flooding, thermal controller malfunction and catalyst degradation as well as data sovereignty across manufacturing plants used.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Driver behavior classification is central to proactive road-safety management, yet smartphone-based approaches still require models that are not only accurate but also stable, computationally efficient, and interpretable. This study addresses this gap by developing an optimized and explainable ensemble-learning framework for classifying slow, normal, and aggressive driving using smartphone accelerometer and gyroscope signals. The dataset was constructed from two public smartphone-based sources and transformed into 5-step temporal windows, producing 30 raw sequential inertial features from six sensor channels. Three tree-based ensemble classifiers, LightGBM, Random Forest (RF), and Extra Trees, were optimized using Bayesian Optimization, Puma Optimization, and Snake-based Optimization, and evaluated using fixed test-set analysis, 30 repeated stratified hold-out runs, statistical testing, runtime comparison, and explainable AI methods. Across repeated test runs, RF optimized by Bayesian Optimization achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy, with accuracy of 0.699 ± 0.014, balanced accuracy of 0.682 ± 0.015, and weighted F1-score of 0.706 ± 0.014. Statistical testing confirmed significant overall differences among model–optimizer configurations using the Friedman test (p < 0.05), while RF–Snake, RF–Puma, and ET–Snake were not significantly different from RF–Bayesian after Holm correction. On the fixed held-out test set, RF–Bayesian achieved balanced accuracy of 0.686 and weighted F1-score of 0.727, with the strongest class-level performance observed for aggressive driving (recall = 0.822 and F1-score = 0.808). The model also showed good probability-based separability. Explainability analyses using permutation importance, SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), and Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs) consistently showed that gyroscope X-axis sequence features, particularly GyroX4, GyroX1, GyroX2, GyroX5, and GyroX3, were the dominant predictors, indicating that short-term rotational dynamics are critical for identifying aggressive driving. These findings demonstrate that RF–Bayesian provides a stable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for smartphone-based driver behavior classification, with practical relevance for telematics, fleet safety management, driver feedback systems, and intelligent transportation safety applications.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The residential sector accounts for a major share of global electricity demand, and this demand is projected to rise sharply with the spread of automated appliances and heatwave-driven cooling loads. While fuzzy-logic HVAC control, dynamic pricing, and renewable-storage integration have each been studied individually, few works jointly quantify how a fuzzy-logic energy management controller interacts with real-time and time-of-use pricing and with renewable generation, storage, and load shifting within a single, reproducible residential simulation framework, leaving the combined saving potential and its attribution across mechanisms unclear. This study addresses that gap by developing a fuzzy-logic-based energy management controller for an interruptible HVAC load and a smart load simulator (SLS)–based model of critical and noncritical residential loads, evaluated under real-time pricing (RTP) and time-of-use (TOU) tariffs with and without local solar PV, wind, and battery storage. A MATLAB/Simulink GUIDE-based platform was used to run the simulations over a representative one-month operating horizon, with a 72-rule fuzzy inference base built on four input variables: outdoor temperature, price, demand, and occupancy. Simulation results show that the fuzzy HVAC controller reduces HVAC energy consumption by approximately 28% relative to manual thermostat operation under RTP and that combining renewable generation with noncritical load shifting reduces total household energy consumption and cost by 42.28% and 38.37%, respectively. The contribution of this work is a unified, reproducible residential energy management framework that jointly evaluates fuzzy HVAC control, dynamic-pricing response, and renewable-storage-shifting strategies within one consistent simulation environment, providing quantitative guidance for residential demand-side management design.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: In this study, we have prepared N and O co-doped porous carbon from walnut shells and significantly improved its physico-chemical properties by a two-step chemical activation approach using ZnCl2 and KOH. The synergistic effect of ZnCl2 and KOH activation resulted in a well-developed hierarchical porous architecture with a high specific surface area (901 m2.g−1) and abundant O and N functional groups, as confirmed by XPS analysis. These features facilitated efficient ion transport and enhanced charge storage capacity. Tested in a three-electrode supercapacitor configuration using a 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte, the optimized carbon electrode exhibited a high specific capacitance of 520 F·g−1 at 1 A·g−1, and outstanding cycling stability over 5000 cycles with a capacity retention greater than 99%. This work presents a sustainable and efficient route to designing high-performance electrode materials from biowaste for next-generation energy storage devices.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs) are increasingly used to localise the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet their governance role in African cities remains poorly understood. This study examines how VLRs shape SDG implementation and the institutional factors influencing their effectiveness through a qualitative content analysis of 30 VLRs covering 30 African cities and 9 African countries. The findings show that VLR adoption is uneven and depends on institutional capacity, national policy frameworks, external support, and data systems. Beyond monitoring progress, VLRs strengthen planning, stakeholder engagement, and multi-level coordination, although their effectiveness is constrained by limited institutional and technical capacity. The study proposes a multi-level governance framework and highlights the need to strengthen local institutions, data systems, and intergovernmental coordination to advance SDG localisation in Africa.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) comprise thousands of anthropogenic fluorinated compounds whose exceptional stability conferred by the carbon–fluorine bond, the strongest single bond in organic chemistry has earned them the epithet “forever chemicals.” Decades of use in aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF), industrial processes, and consumer products have created persistent, highly mobile groundwater plumes that are now detected on every inhabited continent. The promulgation of the first legally binding U.S. drinking water limits (4 ng/L for PFOA and PFOS) in 2024, and the regulatory controversy that followed in 2025–2026, have transformed PFAS from an emerging concern into an urgent remediation imperative. This review critically synthesizes contemporary knowledge of PFAS occurrence, geochemical behaviour, and remediation in groundwater, and is organized around a central argument: the field is undergoing a paradigm shift from sequestration to destruction. We first examine sources and subsurface transport, highlighting the physicochemical controls air–water interfacial adsorption, precursor transformation, and matrix interactions that govern plume evolution and complicate site characterization. We then show that the prevailing sequestration technologies (granular activated carbon, ion exchange, and high-pressure membranes) concentrate rather than destroy PFAS, generating problematic residual streams. Against this backdrop, the rapidly developing suite of destruction technologies, electrochemical oxidation, UV/sulfite reductive defluorination by hydrated electrons, supercritical water oxidation, plasma-based treatment, sonolysis, and base-mediated low-temperature mineralization is critically appraised using a common set of criteria: defluorination efficiency, by-product formation, energy demand, and field readiness. A multi-criteria comparison shows that no single technology is superior across all criteria, and that separation and destruction are most rationally deployed as complementary stages of an integrated “concentrate-then-destroy” treatment train. The principal contribution of this review is to place that paradigm on a quantitative footing. We develop a first-order energy model, E_total = E_sep + E_d/CF, which expresses the energy demand of a complete train as a function of the concentration factor CF and thereby reinterprets technology selection in energetic terms. The model yields an explicit design criterion—a technology-specific break-even concentration factor, CF* = E_d/E_sep that identifies how much concentration each destruction route requires before it ceases to dominate the energy budget, and shows that beyond this point the separation step governs whole-train energy. Energy is not the sole determinant of technology choice, and the framework is therefore applied alongside defluorination extent, by-product formation, technology readiness, cost, and matrix compatibility. A simple energy model formalizes this logic, showing that concentration is what renders destruction energetically viable and that, beyond a technology-specific break-even concentration factor, it is the separation step that governs the energy budget of the whole train. We close by identifying priority research needs, including validated destruction metrics, management of short-chain compounds and precursors, and treatment-train optimization. The field's central challenge is no longer removing PFAS from water, but transforming them—cost-effectively and verifiably into harmless fluoride.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Photocatalysis is well defined in the IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (Gold Book); however, photothermal catalysis remains insufficiently defined, and the relative contributions of thermal and nonthermal (photochemical) effects continue to be actively debated. In particular, the interpretation of plasmonic photocatalysis has raised fundamental questions regarding the roles of photothermal heating and generated hot carriers in light-driven processes over plasmonic metal nanoparticles. This perspective paper summarizes a recently recommended classification of thermo-photocatalysis, with specific emphasis on plasmonic photocatalytic systems. The elementary photo-induced processes occurring in plasmonic nanoparticles—including light absorption, localized surface plasmon resonance excitation, hot-carrier generation and relaxation, and nanoscale heat dissipation—are outlined. Representative experimental examples are discussed to illustrate synergistic interactions between thermal and nonthermal pathways in plasmonic photocatalysis. In addition, simple and widely accessible experimental strategies used to distinguish nonthermal contributions—such as analyses of light intensity effects, wavelength-dependent studies, competitive electron transfer reactions, and kinetic isotopic effects—are briefly discussed. By highlighting both the strengths and limitations of these experimental approaches, this paper aims to provide a conceptual framework for distinguishing thermal and nonthermal phenomena and to promote more rigorous mechanistic analyses in future studies of plasmonic and related photo-driven catalytic systems at elevated temperatures.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) platforms can greatly extend healthcare reach in humanitarian settings, delivering vital services to populations in remote regions. Yet limited network infrastructure in such areas hampers conventional IoT deployments. We propose a real-time chest-X-ray classification framework tailored for rural hospitals. The system couples a fine-tuned ResNet50 model for disease recognition with FastDDS middleware to maintain low-latency, reliable communication between clinicians and the inference node. The network attains 88.61% accuracy, 88.76% precision, and 88.49% recall, while end-to-end tests record an average throughput of 3.2 KB/s and a round-trip latency of 65 ms. These outcomes illustrate how middleware-enabled edge inference can support physicians working in connectivity-constrained environments.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: A theoretical framework is developed for graded multi-resonant piezoelectric metastructures with two independently tunable electromechanical resonances per unit cell, realized by a second-order ladder shunt—the electromechanical analog of a two-degree-of-freedom resonator—which opens two locally resonant bandgaps. Using Euler–Bernoulli beam theory and an assumed-modes formulation, closed-form expressions for the bandgap edge frequencies are derived in the infinite-electrode limit and confirmed by plane-wave expansion and finite-element simulations. An exact bandwidth-conservation relation shows that the total bandgap width is fixed by the primary resonance and the electromechanical coupling alone, while the secondary resonance and capacitance ratio only redistribute it between the two gaps. Spatially grading both resonances substantially widens the attenuation band: at a grading parameter ε=0.07 the two-resonance metastructure reaches an attenuation bandwidth of 263.6 Hz versus 180.1 Hz for its single-resonance counterpart. The graded system also exhibits dual rainbow trapping—two simultaneous wave-localization branches in the frequency–position plane—so that each region traps two distinct frequencies. This enhanced localization increases the distributed harvesting potential by up to 9.9% under idealized cell-wise electrical loading at ε=0.05, and by about 2% under a fixed passive load.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The development of advanced sorbent materials for CO₂ capture has progressed rapidly over the past two decades; however, translating laboratory-scale performance into deployable technologies remains a major scientific and engineering challenge. This review provides a comprehensive and critically integrated framework for sorbent design, spanning molecular mechanisms of adsorption, structure–property relationships, kinetic and thermodynamic constraints, and system-level performance under realistic operating conditions. We systematically compare major sorbent classes, including activated carbons, zeolites, and amine-functionalized silicas, and evaluate their performance across key metrics such as adsorption capacity, selectivity, adsorption enthalpy, cyclic stability, and regeneration energy. Beyond conventional material-centric perspectives, we emphasize the importance of multiscale characterization, computational modelling, and operando techniques in resolving adsorption mechanisms under working conditions. We further identify persistent gaps in scalability, standardization, and durability in complex gas environments, which continue to limit industrial translation. Finally, we outline emerging directions, including machine learning–guided materials discovery, stimuli-responsive sorbents, and circular carbon capture (CC) frameworks that integrate separation with resource recovery. Collectively, this work provides a unified perspective linking fundamental adsorption science with practical deployment requirements for next-generation CC technologies.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Healthcare environments present uniquely demanding constraints for the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI). Clinical decisions of significant consequence are rarely the product of a single isolated computation; rather, safe and effective patient care relies on the continuous collaboration of distributed entities, including clinicians, hospital networks, laboratory systems, monitoring devices, and patients themselves. As generative models and large language models are increasingly deployed in clinical settings, the transition from monolithic AI models to Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offers unprecedented capabilities for distributed monitoring, coordinated decision support, and service integration. However, multi-agent collaboration simultaneously introduces severe novel vulnerabilities, including topological contamination, privacy leakage, cascading systemic failures, and the socio-psychological risks of undue algorithmic persuasion. This work introduces a comprehensive, privacy-preserving, explainable, and human-centred MAS framework explicitly designed for collaborative clinical decision support. Rejecting the paradigm of a single, omniscient AI model with unrestricted data access, the proposed architecture operationalises clinical AI as a heavily regulated team of specialised, interacting agents. The framework defines six distinct agent classes: Data Stewardship, Modality, Explanation, Consensus, Safety Monitor, and Clinician Interface agents. Furthermore, the implementation is governed by six foundational design principles grounded in classic Autonomous Agents and MAS theory, adapted for modern generative systems. By enforcing minimum-necessary data exchange, verifiable team-level explainability, explicit hierarchical escalation, secure communication topologies, and human-centred safety protocols, this framework provides both a domain-grounded blueprint and a transferable set of robust design principles for deploying trustworthy MAS in high-stakes environments.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Lost circulation is a major technical bottleneck restricting safe and efficient while-drilling plugging operations. Polyacrylamide gel has become a widely used plugging material in drilling engineering. Unlike rigid, cement-like plugging materials, the gel system formed in this study does not develop a hardened, consolidated structure capable of anchoring or binding the drill bit during subsequent drilling operations, thereby eliminating the risk of bit-sticking. Nevertheless, the gel possesses sufficient elastic (viscoelastic) structural strength—reflected in its storage modulus (G′)—to effectively resist deformation and displacement under differential pressure, thereby providing reliable fracture-sealing performance, which effectively prevents pipe-sticking risks. However, high-concentration PAM molecular chains easily stretch and entangle in aqueous solution, triggering an abnormal increase in initial viscosity and poor pumpability. Although Ca2+ can inhibit the premature water absorption and thickening of PAM to maintain system fluidity, an excessively high Ca2+ concentration will suppress the hydrolysis of Al3+ and hinder the formation of hydroxyaluminum—the key crosslinking component of the gel system. To solve the above contradiction, a CaCl2-tolerant delayed-release crosslinker was synthesized. ZnO was selected as a carrier to adsorb and immobilize polynuclear hydroxyaluminum complexes hydrolyzed from an inorganic aluminum crosslinker at 70 °C, realizing the controlled delayed release of the crosslinker. The microstructures and chemical bonding were characterized by SEM elemental mapping, FT-IR and 27Al MAS NMR. The results confirm that abundant aluminum species are uniformly loaded on the ZnO surface to form stable Zn–O–Al covalent bonds, and the loaded aluminum exists mainly in the form of hydroxyaluminum. With increasing temperature, the Zn–O–Al bonds gradually break and slowly release hydroxyaluminum species. A novel delayed crosslinking gel system was ultimately optimized, composed of 6% CaCl2, 10.4% PAM and 3% ZnO loaded with polynuclear hydroxyaluminum. The system exhibits excellent delayed gelation behavior, with a fluidity loss time longer than 120 min and a gelation time over 200 min. It maintains favorable fluidity within 30–90 °C, and the formed gel shows a stable elastic modulus (G′) and viscous modulus (G″). Moreover, the system achieves a plugging rate of more than 90% and a breakthrough pressure above 5 MPa, demonstrating superior comprehensive plugging performance for while-drilling plugging applications.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Rare metal exploration increasingly relies on the integration of heterogeneous geological datasets and advanced analytical methods to improve the efficiency and reliability of mineral prospecting. This study presents the development of a web-based Geographic Information System, Geospatial Information System for Optimized Rare Metal Exploration in Eastern Kazakhstan (GISORMEK), using the central part of the Kalba–Narym rare-metal belt (Eastern Kazakhstan) as a case study. A comprehensive geospatial database was developed through the digitization of archival geological maps and the integration of geological, geochemical, tectonic, geophysical, geomorphological, and mineral occurrence datasets. To complement historical mapping data, Landsat-8 multispectral imagery was incorporated to improve lithological discrimination and identify hydrothermal alteration zones. Two remote sensing techniques were applied: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for lithological mapping and enhancement of geological features, and band ratio (BR) analysis for the calculation of geological spectral indices, including the iron oxide index and the hydroxyl-bearing (Al–OH) mineral index. The resulting spectral indices were subsequently integrated to generate a predictive hydrothermal alteration map. GISORMEK integrates historical and contemporary datasets within a unified web-GIS framework, ensuring spatial consistency, reproducibility, and accessibility. The proposed framework enhances the interpretation of the mineralization potential of the Kalba–Narym region and provides geospatial platform for supporting rare metal exploration and future mineral prospectivity assessments.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The growing demand for environmentally responsible products has challenged dual-channel retailing and necessitates innovative policies that align economic and environmental objectives. This study introduces a coordinated production–delivery framework that optimizes green technology integration and pricing decisions to enhance supply chain profitability in a dual-channel setting. We consider a manufacturer that implements smart production and invests in greenhouse gas emissions reduction technology (GERT), while the retailer employs information disclosure technology (IDT) to share real-time information bilaterally. We demonstrate that in a decentralized setting with information asymmetry, consumer prices rise and supply chain profits decline owing to an intensified bullwhip-effect. Conversely, a centralized approach with bilateral information sharing and GERT–IDT investment delivers a win–win outcome, reducing online prices by 16.16% and offline prices by 25.67% while increasing demand by 2.16%, in support of SDG 12. Owing to the mixed-integer nonlinear nature of the integrated profit-optimization problem, a hybrid analytic–metaheuristic solution approach is applied, which reduces the bullwhip-effect by 15.62% and increases profit by 1.73%. Sensitivity analyses reveal that transparent information sharing and green investment yield economic savings of up to 20% by minimizing overproduction and inventory costs. The analysis further indicates that, without technology integration, coordination offers only marginal profit improvement.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The Growing energy crisis and environmental destruction worldwide demand the development of technologies for sustainable energy conversion. Photocatalysis is a promising process for hydrogen production and carbon dioxide reduction, but single photocatalysts often suffer from fast charge recombination and weak light absorption. This review focuses on the new type of synergistic composites that are composed of MXenes and Covalent Organic Frameworks. Based on the outstanding metallic conductivity and hydrophilicity of 2D MXenes and the high porosity and light-harvesting versatility of COFs, these hybrid materials are useful in creating superior S-scheme heterojunctions. We examine the basic processes of accelerated charge separation and electron transfer that have made them excel in their photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, CO2 reduction, and organic pollutant degradation. Additionally, the contribution of structural engineering, which includes layer-by-layer self-assembly and intercalation, to the improvement of molecular selectivity and stability is discussed. This review establishes the potential change of MXene-COF platforms in addressing the gap between the basic science of materials and the practicality of solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Moreover, the advanced in situ/operando characterization methods, interface engineering and techno-economic analysis are emphasized for the understanding of reaction mechanisms and promoting practical use of MXene-COF photocatalysts. We end by outlining the existing challenges and give a roadmap at the strategic level of how highly efficient, stable, and scalable MXene-COF photocatalytic systems should progress to achieve a sustainable future.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: As sustainable substitutes for traditional fossil fuel-based agricultural product drying techniques, solar drying technologies have drawn more attention in recent times. A vast and intricate body of knowledge has been produced by the quick expansion of scientific publications in this field, which calls for methodical assessment. In order to map the continental and global research landscape of mixed-mode solar dryer technologies, this study provides a thorough bibliometric analysis. To find publication trends, influential journals, collaboration networks, thematic clusters, and new research directions, 214 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2015 and 2026 were taken from the Scopus database & Web of Science and analysed using Bibliometrix (R-tool) and VOSviewer. The findings show that research output has increased significantly over the past ten years, with Asia, especially India, emerging as the top contributor to solar drying research. The analysis also shows how basic experimental studies are giving way to interdisciplinary research that incorporates digital modelling techniques, sustainability assessment, and thermodynamics. There are still challenges with scalability, cost optimisation, and climate adaptability despite significant technological advancements. To increase system reliability, future research should concentrate on the development of sustainable and economic thermal storage materials, smart control techniques, and hybrid renewable systems. According to the research, community-scale solar drying facilities can greatly lower post-harvest losses, enhance rural livelihoods, and promote sustainable agricultural processing in line with international clean-energy and climate goals in high solar-irradiance regions such as South Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Random lasing in zinc oxide (ZnO) is strongly influenced by nanoscale morphology. Here, one-dimensional (1D) ZnO nanorods were synthesized by chemical bath deposition on a ZnO seed layer, while two-dimensional (2D) ZnO nanowalls were grown on a DC-sputtered Al metal seed layer. Both morphologies exhibit comparable crystallite sizes (∼56 nm) and a preferred (002) orientation. Photoluminescence shows dominant near-band-edge emission, indicating good optical quality. The optical band gaps extracted from PL are 3.28 eV for nanorods and 3.20 eV for nanowalls, while Tauc analysis from UV-Vis spectra gives apparent optical band gaps of 3.22 eV and 3.75 eV, respectively. The higher apparent value obtained for the nanowalls reflects changes in the absorption edge, which may be influenced by band-tail disorder, surface states, and Al-related carrier effects. Under optical pumping, the 1D nanorods show predominantly single-mode random lasing with thresholds of 3.82-4.20 mJ/cm2. In contrast, the 2D nanowalls exhibit position-dependent single-mode, dual-mode, and three-mode random lasing with generally lower thresholds of 2.55-3.48 mJ/cm2. Fourier transform analysis reveals position-dependent optical cavity lengths, indicating that different recurrent scattering paths are formed at different excitation positions. These results suggest that the interconnected 2D ZnO nanowalls interconnected network contributes to more efficient optical feedback than the 1D nanorods, contributing to reduced random lasing thresholds and diverse lasing mode behavior. This work highlights morphology-driven design routes for low-cost ZnO-based photonic light sources.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based acceleration for 3-D object detection has attracted significant attention due to its potential for high efficiency and low latency. However, existing fully sparse 3-D Transformer accelerators suffer from inefficient dataflows and limited parallelism, mainly caused by irregular sparsity patterns and global attention dependencies. To address these challenges, this work introduces the fully sparse Transformer pipeline (FST-PIPE). FST-PIPE adopts a hybrid-grained pipeline that integrates coarse-grained inter-layer streaming with fine-grained intra-operator parallelism, and incorporates a memory-efficient storage design to maximize parallelism and memory efficiency. FST-PIPE is enabled by restructuring global sparse attention into an axis-aligned representation through the proposed AxisFormer block, thereby enabling efficient modeling of long-range dependencies among spatially distant nonempty voxels. Furthermore, this work introduces a length-aware pipeline scheduling mechanism to address workload imbalance arising from variable sequence lengths, eliminating pipeline bubbles and sustaining high hardware utilization. Implemented on a ZCU102 FPGA, FST-PIPE achieves 42.59 frames/s with a latency of 23.48 ms and an energy efficiency of 9.5 frames/s/W, providing up to 1.45x higher throughput and around 2x better energy efficiency compared with prior FPGA-based accelerators.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The overexploitation of groundwater resources is a significant concern due to the potential risks associated with a decline in freshwater availability. Future planning and policymaking should consider long-term groundwater availability and urban expansion patterns to understand urban growth. This study aims to investigate the impact of land cover change on groundwater depletion. Further, the land surface temperature (LST) and vegetation change using Normalized Difference Vegetation Index NDVI analysis have been performed to find the spatial spread of urbanization and its impact on surface temperature in the area. For groundwater assessment, the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) data have been used, while for land cover, NDVI, and LST assessment, Landsat data have been used. The GRACE-based groundwater storage (GWS) anomaly has been correlated with Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) data. An annual groundwater storage decline of ~7.01 mm/year was identified. Groundwater and land-cover changes were evaluated at five-year intervals from 1990 to 2025. The urban expansion from 838 to 1470 km2 coverage shows the rapid expansion and its impact on vegetation and groundwater recharge in the area. The results demonstrate a rapid increase in the urban area, which affected the vegetation and increased the surface temperature in the area. Urban expansion reduced vegetation cover and infiltration, contributing to elevated land surface temperature and groundwater depletion. This study focused on integrating the groundwater impacts due to other environmental variables, i.e., temperature increase and vegetation decrease. The temporal increase in urban expansion decreases the infiltration rate, which impacts the groundwater storage and depletion, as shown by the linear trend. These findings underscore the urgent need for effective groundwater management and vegetation management policies and integrated urban planning strategies to ensure the long-term sustainability of freshwater resources.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Heavy metal (HM) pollution is a traditional and ongoing global ecological issue that requires continuous attention. Although studies have focused on how plants cope with HMs stress, the related results ineffectively serve phytoremediation and control HMs toxicity. Melatonin (MT), as a multifunctional signaling molecule, has significant potential in alleviating HMs toxicity in crops. In this meta-analysis, a dataset across different plant families comprising 2476 observations from 140 studies evaluates MT-mediated crosstalk regulating plant growth under HMs stress. Results revealed that exogenous MT significantly improved overall plant performance by 18% (95% CI = 19.5%–14.8%), including plant growth (41.4%), morphology (51.3%) and physiology (44.4%) by stimulating shoot and root biomass 45.5% and 39.5%, respectively. The marked increment in chlorophyll (33.6%) and antioxidant activities (31.8%) was observed by mitigating the adverse effects of oxidative damage (− 23.5%). The elevated nutrient acquisition (24%) and endogenous MT level (59%) were accompanied by 24.2% increase in metabolites and -19.4% reduction in HMs uptake. Random forest machine learning revealed that plant species, MT duration and HMs concentration were the dominant predictors of biomass, whereas HMs type and exposure duration followed by MT level and duration exerted significant influence on plant length and oxidative stress. These effects were significantly associated with MT-mediated genes response and dose or exposure duration, where MT ≤ 100 μM for ≤ 15 days significantly improved results, while excessive level of HMs and prolonged exposure duration diminished MT efficacy. These findings underscore the promising potential of MT-mediated mechanisms in attenuating the injurious effects of HMs on plants.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Plastic waste recycling has become an important pathway for reducing landfill dependence, conserving resources, and supporting circular economy transitions, particularly in arid regions where high material demand, harsh climatic conditions, and limited recycling infrastructure can constrain waste recovery. This review develops a technology-selection framework for plastic waste recycling in Qatar, with relevance to Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and other arid-region economies. The review synthesizes literature on plastic waste feedstocks, mechanical and chemical recycling routes, solvent-assisted recycling, pelletization, construction materials, additive manufacturing, life cycle assessment, techno-economic performance, digital enablers, and Qatar/GCC-specific implementation challenges. The analysis indicates that recycling pathways should not be evaluated solely on the basis of direct environmental burdens, but also in relation to feedstock quality, contamination level, recyclate performance, virgin-material substitution potential, processing cost, and end-use requirements. Mechanical recycling and pelletization are generally preferred for clean and separated polyethylene and polypropylene streams because of their lower processing complexity and higher commercial maturity. However, mixed, contaminated, or compatibility-limited plastic waste may require advanced sorting, compatibilization, solvent-assisted recycling, or selected chemical recycling routes to recover material value. Recycled plastics show potential in construction materials, fiber-reinforced systems, recycled filaments, oil sorbents, activated carbon composites, and other functional products; however, quality loss, microplastic generation, durability uncertainty, standardization gaps, and scale-up limitations continue to present important challenges. Digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, Internet of Things systems, and digital twins, can improve sorting accuracy, material traceability, process control, and lifecycle decision-making. Overall, the review emphasizes that circular plastic recycling in Qatar and similar arid regions requires feedstock-specific technology selection, life cycle and techno-economic assessment, localized recycling infrastructure, quality standards, and coordinated policy support.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Accelerated carbonation curing (ACC) has attracted increasing attention as a curing technique for concrete masonry units (CMUs) because it can simultaneously accelerate strength development and utilize CO2. Unlike conventional steam curing, ACC introduces controlled CO2 exposure during the curing stage of freshly formed masonry products, enabling strength development and permanent carbon sequestration. This paper reviews the current research on ACC of load-bearing and non-load-bearing CMUs, including manufacturing methods, mix design, curing parameters, CO₂ uptake, mechanical properties, durability, and industrial implementation. Evidence from laboratory-scale specimens, and pilot- and full-scale block production is examined to identify the governing mechanisms and practical performance trends. The reviewed studies show that ACC can permanently sequester approximately 9–25% of cement mass as CO2 in OPC-based systems, while reducing curing-energy demand from approximately 2500 kJ/block for steam curing to about 500 kJ/block. Across the literature, the optimum moisture condition consistently corresponded to approximately 4–6% residual moisture or 35–50% mixing-water loss, confirming that moisture pre-conditioning is the dominant process variable controlling carbonation efficiency. The reviewed studies also demonstrate that low-pressure carbonation curing, typically about 0.1–0.5 bar above atmospheric pressure and 2–6 h duration, is generally sufficient for practical masonry production. ACC is shown to provide substantial early-age strength gain and CO2 uptake, although maximum sequestration and maximum strength do not necessarily coincide under the same curing conditions. The review also shows that post-carbonation hydration is important for later-age performance, and that ACC generally improves dimensional stability and reduces water transport, while long-term durability evidence remains comparatively limited. Alternative and low-clinker binder systems, including recycled-aggregate fines, slag-based, and waste-derived masonry products, further demonstrate the broader potential of ACC, but their scale-up and standardization are less mature than those of OPC-based systems. Overall, ACC is a feasible alternative to steam curing for masonry production. ACC can reduce energy consumption and permanently store CO2 in masonry products. However, wider industrial application still requires standardized curing methods, long-term durability verification, and optimization of plant-scale curing processes.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Developing coke-resistant, cost-effective catalysts for methane-to-syngas conversion using air remains challenging. Herein, we report a one-pot colloidal solution combustion synthesis (CSC) to synthesize nanocrystalline Ni/CeO2 featuring highly dispersed Ni, abundant oxygen-vacancies, and a well-developed Ni-Ce-O interface. Extensive characterization including XRD, HR-TEM, XPS, O2-TPD, CH4-TPD/TPSR, H2-TPR, EPR and Raman elucidated the structural, redox, and defect features imparted by the CSC synthesis method. TEM confirmed uniformly distributed Ni nanoparticles embedded within the ceria matrix. CH4-TPSR revealed early CO2 and H2O formation at ~210 °C, indicating low-temperature CH4 activation by oxygen species. In-situ Raman spectroscopy revealed abundant oxygen vacancies and their active participation during methane activation, while in-situ DRIFTS identified surface formate and carbonate intermediates, confirming an oxygen-assisted reaction pathway. The optimized 5Ni/CeO2 catalyst achieved 99% methane conversion with nearly 100% syngas selectivity at 700 °C. Raman and TGA/DTG analyses confirmed excellent coke resistance and stable performance throughout 300 h of testing.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Integrating photovoltaic/thermal (PVT) cooling with proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis offers a promising approach for green hydrogen generation by simultaneously recovering the low-grade thermal energy and improving photovoltaic electrical performance. Despite its potential, the performance of integrated PVT-PEM systems under high irradiance and high temperature conditions typical of arid regions has not been sufficiently investigated. This study experimentally evaluates the hybrid PVT-PEM system under outdoor conditions in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia. The system was instrumented to continuously record solar irradiance, electrical power, coolant flow rate, temperature, and hydrogen production rate. The experimental results show that PVT cooling increases PV electrical efficiency by 6 to 12% relative to an uncooled PV system, with the largest improvement observed under high solar irradiance and subsequently high surface PV temperature. Consequently, hydrogen production rates increase up to 10% at high solar irradiance levels. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that increasing the coolant flow rate raises the recovered thermal power from 0.6 kW to 1.3 kW and improves the PV electrical efficiency from 13% to 14.5%. The maximum solar-to-hydrogen efficiency achieved by the PVT-cooled system was 10.2% compared with 9.2% for the uncooled configuration, corresponding to an 11% improvement. Under average operating conditions, the PVT system delivered approximately 450 W of electrical power and 2000 W of recovered thermal power, corresponding to electrical, thermal, and overall PVT efficiencies of 14%, 50%, and 62%, respectively, evaluated at ṁ = 0.05 kg s−1. The average specific energy consumption for hydrogen production is about 45 kWh/kg. In addition, the proposed system is estimated to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 1.65–1.88 tCO2/year, or 49.39 – 56.46 tCO2 over a period of 30-year lifetime. These outcomes clearly highlight that the PEM-PVT hybrid system is a promising solution for producing both green hydrogen and useful heat energy, enhancing solar energy utilization and supporting sustainable energy transitions in hot-arid regions.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study investigates the effect of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium salt dihydrate (EDTA) on the reactivity of SiO2 nanoparticles in a Ca(OH)2–SiO2 system. In calcium-containing aqueous solutions, SiO2 nanoparticles tend to coagulate due to calcium ion adsorption, reducing their reactivity in lime-based systems. EDTA was used as a calcium chelator to temporarily reduce free calcium ions during the early mixing stage. Dynamic light scattering, isothermal calorimetry, thermogravimetric analysis, and compressive strength tests were conducted to evaluate different EDTA dosages. The results showed that EDTA enhanced the ultimate reactivity of SiO2 nanoparticles, with the 250 mM EDTA system exhibiting the highest cumulative heat release. Although EDTA reduced the nucleation and growth reaction rate and increased the apparent activation energy, mixtures containing EDTA achieved higher compressive strength than the control system without EDTA. Thermogravimetric analysis further confirmed the calorimetry findings, indicating enhanced nanoparticle consumption and greater reaction product formation overall during curing.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) for crystal property prediction are typically evaluated by a single aggregate error, which can mask where, and for which classes of materials, these models fail. In this study, we present a space-group-, centering-type-, and band gap-resolved error analysis of GNN band gap prediction on the Materials Project dataset. As a channel for this analysis we use Crystal-X, a deliberately simple model: a standard graph convolutional backbone with two minor architectural modifications, an asymmetric edge convolution and a neighbor-feature transformation, that supplement bond information often treated as secondary in node-centric models. Crystal-X is not a state-of-the-art model: it reaches a band gap MAE of 0.256 eV on the MP 2018.6 dataset, behind ALIGNN (0.22 eV) and PotNet (0.20 eV), though ahead of older baselines such as CGCNN (0.39 eV), SchNet (0.415 eV), and MEGNet (0.33 eV) while using only the nine-property CGCNN atomic feature set. Its value here is as a controlled, low-complexity testbed for the error analysis. That analysis reveals systematic patterns that aggregate MAE conceals: errors concentrate in underrepresented band gap ranges and in low-symmetry and non-centrosymmetric space groups; per-group errors for sparsely populated space groups are dominated by sampling noise; and modest, as-yet-unverified gains from edge-aware convolutions appear in monoclinic and non-primitive-centered systems. We argue that this kind of granular, symmetry-resolved evaluation should accompany aggregate benchmarks when assessing crystal GNNs.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Hydrogen is a promising alternative energy source as the world moves toward decarbonization by reducing reliance on traditional fossil fuels. This review encompasses a comprehensive study of emerging materials for hydrogen storage, beginning with the physical and thermodynamic properties of hydrogen and the need for effective hydrogen storage solutions. Solid-state storage has attracted considerable attention because of its greater capacity and improved safety. Advancements in materials design have yielded many hydrogen storage candidates, including nanostructured materials, carbon-based nanostructures, metal–organic frameworks, porous carbon, MXenes, metal halides, functional polymers, and porous organic polymers. These materials offer many advantages but also pose important concerns, such as limited storage capacity, slow response, and ongoing structural deterioration. Moreover, the combination of polymers and nanostructured materials has emerged as an attractive solution to address these concerns. This type of hybrid material improves surface chemistry, pore architecture, stability, and enhances hydrogen uptake and kinetics. The potential implementation of hydrogen storage and its associated limitations have been thoroughly discussed.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Molecular aggregates and advanced molecular self-assemblies of polymers are some of the hot topics of research these days. The term molecular aggregates refers to structures containing long chains that are formed by molecular self-assembly through non-covalent interactions i.e., hydrogen bonding, dipole-dipole interactions, π–π interactions, hydrophobic forces, etc. The properties of the resulting molecular aggregate strongly depend on the type of interactions employed within it. On the other hand, advanced molecular self-assemblies include the process of self-assembling components into complex and advanced structures due to interactions of molecules. Molecular aggregates and advanced molecular self-assemblies of polymers have opened new windows to synthesize new polymers and complexes with varying structures and properties through the process of self-assembly that can be utilized in a number of applications. The upper hand of such aggregates and self-assemblies over other structures can be explained in terms of control over the structure, stability, biocompatibility, etc. During the synthesis of complexes and composites using advanced molecular self-assembly techniques, both synthetic and natural polymers can be utilized e.g., in the case of polymer-peptide complexes, synthetic polymers can also be utilized. These molecular aggregates of polymers have enormous applications in the fields of biomedicine, sensing, coating, additive manufacturing, tissue engineering, artificial muscles, gene therapy, electronic materials, energy storage, advanced optics, catalysis, etc. This chapter provides an overview of polymers and molecular aggregates-advanced molecular self-assemblies.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is increasing rapidly. Early detection of BC can improve treatment and decrease the mortality rate. However, BC detection at early stages is challenging due to the complex histopathological tissue structure, variations in staining, and magnification levels. Also, the high morphological similarity among different breast lesion subtypes makes accurate diagnosis difficult. Previous studies have primarily relied on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which effectively capture local tissue features but often fail to model long-range contextual dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose a novel EfficientNet-Attention-Vision Transformer (EffiAtt-ViT) framework for BC detection. We use EfficientNet to extract discriminative multi-scale local tissue features. After that, the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is used to enhance salient channel and spatial feature representations. The Vision Transformer (ViT) is used to capture long-range contextual dependencies among refined feature embeddings. After that, we perform feature fusion by integrating the locally discriminative features extracted by EfficientNet with the globally contextual representations learned by the ViT. This enables the model to maintain detailed cellular morphology while capturing the overall tissue structure. To validate the model performance, we use two publicly available datasets, known as Breast Cancer Histopathological Image Classification (BreakHis) and the Breast Cancer Histology images (BACH) dataset. We obtained an accuracy of 98.45% using BreakHis and 95.39% using the BACH dataset, outperforming closely related works. This work contributes to the existing literature by presenting an optimized EffiAtt-ViT framework that integrates multi-scale feature extraction, attention-guided learning, and global contextual modeling for breast histopathology image classification.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The Environmental Phillips Curve (EPC) has recently been tested for several economies and regions. However, the EPC hypothesis has yet to be tested for the Chinese economy. Accordingly, this research study assesses the EPC hypothesis in China, exploring whether unemployment dynamics influence environmental degradation during China’s transition toward greener economic growth. Utilizing data from 1991–2023, the study employs the ARDL methodology to evaluate the EPC hypothesis in both long and short run dynamics. The ARDL results validate the EPC, revealing a negative and statistically significant association between unemployment and environmental degradation. Granger causality tests further confirmed unidirectional causality from unemployment to environmental degradation. Additionally, the findings affirm the classic inverted U-shaped EKC for China, while highlighting the detrimental influences of traditional energy consumption and trade openness on environmental quality. These insights offer valuable policy guidance, marking this as the pioneering study to rigorously test the EPC hypothesis in China.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) vehicles rely on distributed propulsion (DP) to achieve efficiency, control authority, and compact integration with lifting surfaces. The close spacing of multiple rotors, however, intensifies installation effects that elevate tonal and broadband noise. This work presents a high-fidelity Large Eddy Simulation (LES) study using the CABARET method on rotating meshes to quantify aeroacoustic and aerodynamic sensitivities of a three-propeller DP configuration. The campaign varies: (i) central-rotor axial position (∆ = {−0.2, 0, +0.2}), (ii) inter-rotor phase angle (0°, 45°, 90°, 135°), and(iii) blade trailing-edge geometry (baseline vs. sawtooth serrations). Band-limited overall sound pressure level (BL OASPL) is evaluated on a probe plane under the array between the 1st and 6th blade-passing frequencies. Key findings are: (a) serrations consistently reduce area-averaged and maximum BL OASPL by up to 2.4 dB, most notably around 90◦ phase; (b) moving the central rotor closer to the wing increases thrust coefficient by ≈ 7.8%, indicating a beneficial rotor–wing interaction akin to ground effect; (c) the aerodynamic penalty of serrations is modest and attributable to effective area loss near the tip. Flow visualizations show serrations disrupt spanwise coherence and trailing-edge vortex organization, explaining the observed acoustic benefits. The results highlight the importance of joint optimization of geometry and phasing to deliver quieter, efficient DP systems for UAM.
